text: In a screw gauge when the circular scale is given five complete rotations it moves linearly by 2.5 mm . If the circular scale has 100 divisions, the least count of screw gauge is $____$ mm.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The pitch of a screw gauge is defined as the linear distance moved by the screw on the main scale when the circular head is given one complete rotation.

The screw moves linearly by 2.5 mm when given five complete rotations. Therefore, the distance moved in a single rotation is :

$\text{Pitch}=\frac{\text{Total linear distance moved}}{\text{Number of full rotations}}$

$\text{Pitch}=\frac{2.5\mathrm{mm}}{5}=0.5\mathrm{mm}$

The least count is the smallest distance that can be measured accurately using the instrument. It is the distance moved by the screw when the circular scale is rotated through only one of its divisions.

So, the least count of screw gauge is the ratio of the pitch to the total number of divisions on the circular scale:

It is given that the circular scale has 100 divisions,

L. $\mathrm{C}.=\frac{0.5\mathrm{mm}}{100}=0.005\mathrm{mm}=5\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{mm}$

Therefore, the least count of given screw gauge is $5\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{mm}$. 

Thus, the correct option is (D).

text:
The increase in the pressure required to decrease the volume ( $\Delta V$ ) of water is $6.3\times 10^{7}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}^{2}$. The percentage decrease in the volume is $____$ .

(Bulk modulus of water $=2.1\times 10^{9}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}^{2}$.)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When a uniform pressure (or stress) is applied to the surface of a fluid, it undergoes a decrease in volume.

The bulk modulus ( $β$ ) is defined as the ratio of the volumetric stress (change in pressure, $\Delta \mathrm{P}$ ) to the volumetric strain (fractional change in volume, $\frac{\Delta \mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{V}}$ ).

$β=\frac{\Delta P}{\Delta V/V}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\Delta \mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{V}}=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{P}}{β}$

Increase in pressure is $\Delta \mathrm{P}=6.3\times 10^{7}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}^{2}$

Bulk Modulus of water is $β=2.1\times 10^{9}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}^{2}$

Substituting the given values,

$\frac{\Delta V}{V}=\frac{6.3\times 10^{7}}{2.1\times 10^{9}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\Delta \mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{V}}=3\times 10^{-2}$

The percentage decrease in volume is $\left (\frac{\Delta \mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{V}}\right )\times 100$

$\Delta %=\left (3\times 10^{-2}\right )\times 100=3%$

Therefore, the percentage decrease in the volume is $3%$. 

Thus, the correct option is (B).

text: The time taken by a block of mass $m$ to slide down from the highest point to the lowest point on a rough inclined plane is $50%$ more compared to the time taken by the same block on identical inclined smooth plane. Both inclined planes are at $45^{\circ }$ with the horizontal. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the rough inclined surface and block is $____$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For smooth inclined plane :

When the plane is smooth, there is no friction. The only forces acting on the block along the incline are the component of gravity ( $\mathrm{mg}\sin θ$ ).


[IMG]


According to Newton's Second Law :

$\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{net}}=\mathrm{ma}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{mg}\sin θ=\mathrm{ma}_{\mathrm{s}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{s}}=\mathrm{g}\sin θ$

Using the second equation of motion, $S=ut+\frac{1}{2}at^{2}$, where the block starts from rest $(u=0)$ and travels a distance L (length of the incline):

$\mathrm{L}=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{s}}\mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{s}}^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $t_{s}=\sqrt{\frac{2L}{a_{s}}}=\sqrt{\frac{2L}{g\sin θ}}$

For rough inclined plane :

On a rough plane, kinetic friction ( $\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{k}}$ ) acts upwards against the motion.


[IMG]


The normal force is $\mathrm{N}=\mathrm{mg}\cos θ$, so $\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{k}}=μ_{\mathrm{k}}\mathrm{N}=μ_{\mathrm{k}}\mathrm{mg}\cos θ$.

The net force along the incline is :

$\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{net}}=\mathrm{mg}\sin θ-μ_{\mathrm{k}}\mathrm{mg}\cos θ$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{ma}_{\mathrm{r}}=\mathrm{m}(\mathrm{g}\sin θ-μ_{\mathrm{k}}\mathrm{g}\cos θ)$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{r}}=\mathrm{g}(\sin θ-μ_{\mathrm{k}}\cos θ)$

The time taken $\mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{r}}$ to travel the same distance L is:

$t_{r}=\sqrt{\frac{2L}{a_{r}}}=\sqrt{\frac{2L}{g(\sin θ-μ_{k}\cos θ)}}$

It is given that $\mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{r}}$ is $50%$ more than $\mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{s}}$.

$\mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{r}}=\mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{s}}+0.5\mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{s}}=1.5\mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{s}}=\frac{3}{2}\mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{s}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{r}}^{2}=\frac{9}{4}\mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{s}}^{2}$

Substituting the expressions for $\mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{r}}^{2}$ and $\mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{s}}^{2}$ :

$\frac{2L}{g(\sin θ-μ_{k}\cos θ)}=\frac{9}{4}\left (\frac{2L}{g\sin θ}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{\sin θ-μ_{k}\cos θ}=\frac{9}{4\sin θ}$

$\Rightarrow$ $4\sin θ=9\sin θ-9μ_{\mathrm{k}}\cos θ$

$\Rightarrow$ $9μ_{\mathrm{k}}\cos θ=5\sin θ$

$\Rightarrow$ $μ_{\mathrm{k}}=\frac{5}{9}\tan θ$

The angle of inclination is $θ=45^{\circ }$

$μ_{\mathrm{k}}=\frac{5}{9}\tan 45^{\circ }=\frac{5}{9}$

Therefore, the correct option is (C).

text: Two nuclei of mass number 3 combine with another nucleus of mass number 4 to yield a nucleus of mass number 10. If the binding energy per nucleon for the mass numbers 3,4 and 10 are $5.6\mathrm{MeV},7.4\mathrm{MeV}$ and 6.1 MeV , respectively, then in the process, $\Delta \mathrm{Mc}^{2}=$ $____$ MeV .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In nuclear reactions, the energy released or absorbed ( $\Delta \mathrm{Mc}^{2}$ or Q -value) is the difference between the total binding energy of the product nuclei and the total binding energy of the reactant nuclei.

$2X^{3}+Y^{4}\to Z^{10}+Q$

The reactants consist of two nuclei of mass number $\mathrm{A}=3$ and one nucleus of mass number $\mathrm{A}=4$.

Binding energy ( BE) is calculated as, $\mathrm{BE}=($ Binding Energy per nucleon $)\times ($ Mass Number $)$.

For one nucleus of $\mathrm{A}=3:\mathrm{BE}_{3}=3\times 5.6\mathrm{MeV}=16.8\mathrm{MeV}$

For two such nuclei: $2\times \mathrm{BE}_{3}=33.6\mathrm{MeV}$

For one nucleus of $\mathrm{A}=4:\mathrm{BE}_{4}=4\times 7.4\mathrm{MeV}=29.6\mathrm{MeV}$

Total BE of reactants $=33.6+29.6=63.2\mathrm{MeV}$

The product is one nucleus of mass number $\mathrm{A}=10$.

For one nucleus of $\mathrm{A}=10:\mathrm{BE}_{10}=10\times 6.1\mathrm{MeV}=61.0\mathrm{MeV}$

The energy released or the change in mass-energy is :

$\Delta \mathrm{Mc}^{2}=\mathrm{BE}_{\text{products}}-\mathrm{BE}_{\text{reactants}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta \mathrm{Mc}^{2}=61.0\mathrm{MeV}-63.2\mathrm{MeV}=-2.2\mathrm{MeV}$

The negative sign indicates that the process is endothermic, meaning energy must be supplied for the reaction to occur because the product is less stable than the reactants.

Therefore, the magnitude of the energy change in the process is 2.2 MeV . 

Thus, the correct option is (C).

text: A solid sphere of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is divided into two unequal parts. The smaller part having mass $M/8$ is converted into a sphere of radius $r$ and the larger part is converted into a circular disc of thickness $t$ and radius $2R$. If $I_{1}$ is moment of inertia of a sphere having radius $r$ about an axis through its centre and $I_{2}$ is the moment of inertia of a disc about its diameter, the ratio of their moment of inertia $I_{2}/I_{1}=$ $____$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The smaller part has a mass $\mathrm{m}_{1}=\mathrm{M}/8$.

The formed sphere is of radius $r$.

Since the material is the same, the density ( $ρ$ ) remains constant.

The mass of the original sphere is $M=ρ\cdot \frac{4}{3}πR^{3}$.

The mass of the new sphere is $\mathrm{m}_{1}=ρ\cdot \frac{4}{3}π\mathrm{r}^{3}$.

$\frac{\mathrm{m}_{1}}{\mathrm{M}}=\frac{\mathrm{r}^{3}}{\mathrm{R}^{3}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\mathrm{M}/8}{\mathrm{M}}=\left (\frac{\mathrm{r}}{\mathrm{R}}\right )^{3}\Rightarrow \frac{1}{8}=\left (\frac{\mathrm{r}}{\mathrm{R}}\right )^{3}\Rightarrow \mathrm{r}=\frac{\mathrm{R}}{2}$

The moment of inertia of a solid sphere about its central axis is given by :

$I_{1}=\frac{2}{5}m_{1}r^{2}$

Substituting $\mathrm{m}_{1}=\frac{\mathrm{M}}{8}$ and $\mathrm{r}=\frac{\mathrm{R}}{2}$ :

$\mathrm{I}_{1}=\frac{2}{5}\left (\frac{\mathrm{M}}{8}\right )\left (\frac{\mathrm{R}}{2}\right )^{2}=\frac{2}{5}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{M}}{8}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{R}^{2}}{4}=\frac{2\mathrm{MR}^{2}}{160}=\frac{\mathrm{MR}^{2}}{80}$

The larger part has a mass $m_{2}=M-\frac{M}{8}=\frac{7M}{8}$.

This part is converted into a disc of radius $R_{d}=2R$.

The moment of inertia of a disc about its diameter is given by :

$\mathrm{I}_{2}=\frac{1}{4}\mathrm{m}_{2}\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{d}}^{2}$

Substituting $\mathrm{m}_{2}=\frac{7\mathrm{M}}{8}$ and $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{d}}=2\mathrm{R}$ :

$I_{2}=\frac{1}{4}\left (\frac{7M}{8}\right )(2R)^{2}=\frac{1}{4}\times \frac{7M}{8}\times 4R^{2}=\frac{7MR^{2}}{8}$

So, the ratio of moments of inertia is,

$\frac{\mathrm{I}_{2}}{\mathrm{I}_{1}}=\frac{7\mathrm{MR}^{2}/8}{\mathrm{MR}^{2}/80}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\mathrm{I}_{2}}{\mathrm{I}_{1}}=\frac{7}{8}\times 80=7\times 10=70$

Therefore, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text: The two projectiles are projected with the same initial velocities at the $15^{\circ }$ and $30^{\circ }$ with respect to the horizontal. The ratio of their ranges is $1:x$. The value of $x$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When a projectile launched with initial velocity $u$ at an angle $θ$ to the horizontal.


[IMG]


Horizontal component of velocity: $\mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{x}}=\mathrm{u}\cos θ$

Vertical component of velocity: $\mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{y}}=\mathrm{u}\sin θ$

The time of flight ( T ) is the time taken for the vertical displacement to become zero.

Using $\mathrm{s}=\mathrm{ut}+\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{at}^{2}$ for the vertical direction:

$0=(\mathrm{u}\sin θ)\mathrm{T}-\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{gT}^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{T}=\frac{2\mathrm{u}\sin θ}{\mathrm{g}}$

The horizontal range ( R ) is the horizontal distance covered during this time :

$\mathrm{R}=\mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{x}}\cdot \mathrm{T}=(\mathrm{u}\cos θ)\left (\frac{2\mathrm{u}\sin θ}{\mathrm{g}}\right )$

Using the trigonometric identity $2\sin θ\cos θ=\sin θ$ :

$R=\frac{u^{2}\sin 2θ}{g}$

Since the initial velocities ( u ) are the same for both projectiles :

$\mathrm{R}\propto \sin 2θ$

For the first projectile $(θ_{1}=15^{\circ })$ :

$\mathrm{R}_{1}\propto \sin (2\times 15^{\circ })=\sin 30^{\circ }=\frac{1}{2}$

For the second projectile $(θ_{2}=30^{\circ })$ :

$R_{2}\propto \sin (2\times 30^{\circ })=\sin 60^{\circ }=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

Taking the ratio :

$\frac{\mathrm{R}_{1}}{\mathrm{R}_{2}}=\frac{1/2}{\sqrt{3}/2}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{1}{x}\Rightarrow x=\sqrt{3}$

Therefore, the correct option is (B).

text:
The graph shows variation of stopping potential $V_{\mathrm{o}}$ with the frequency $v$ of the incident radiation for three photosensitive metals $X_{1},X_{2}$ and $X_{3}$. Which metal will give out electrons with greater kinetic energy, for the same wavelength of incident radiation?


[IMG]
options: All the metals will give out photo electrons with same kinetic energies.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The Einstein's photoelectric equation states that the energy of incident photons to the work function of the metal and the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons.

$\mathrm{K}_{\max }=\mathrm{h}ν-\Phi _{0}$

Where $\mathrm{K}_{\max }$ is the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons, $\mathrm{h}ν$ is the energy of the incident photon (where h is Planck's constant and $ν$ is frequency) and $\Phi _{0}$ is the work function of the metal, which is the minimum energy required to eject an electron.

The work function can also be expressed in terms of the threshold frequency $(v_{0})$, which is the minimum frequency required for photoelectric emission:

$\Phi _{0}=\mathrm{h}v_{0}$

The stopping potential ( $\mathrm{V}_{0}$ ) is the negative potential applied to stop the most energetic photoelectrons. The work done by this potential equals the maximum kinetic energy:

$\mathrm{K}_{\max }=\mathrm{eV}_{0}$

Substituting this into the photoelectric equation:

$\mathrm{eV}_{0}=\mathrm{h}v-𝜙\Rightarrow \mathrm{V}_{0}=\left (\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{e}}\right )v-\frac{\Phi _{0}}{\mathrm{e}}$

The equation $\mathrm{V}_{0}=\left (\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{e}}\right )v-\Phi _{0}$ is in the form of a straight line $(\mathrm{y}=\mathrm{mx}+\mathrm{c})$.

The slope $\mathrm{m}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{e}}=$ constant for all metals, which is why the lines are parallel.

X -intercept represents the threshold frequency $(v_{0})$, where $\mathrm{V}_{0}=0$. At this frequency, the incident energy exactly equals the work function $(\Phi _{0}=\mathrm{h}ν_{0})$.

From the graph, we can identify the threshold frequencies for each metal:

For $\mathrm{X}_{1}:v_{0}\approx 1.0\times 10^{14}\mathrm{Hz}$

For $\mathrm{X}_{2}:v_{0}\approx 1.5\times 10^{14}\mathrm{Hz}$

For $\mathrm{X}_{3}:v_{0}\approx 2.0\times 10^{14}\mathrm{Hz}$

We can see that $v_{01}<v_{02}<v_{03}$. This means the work function of metal $\mathrm{X}_{1}$ is the lowest $(\Phi _{1}<\Phi _{2}<\Phi _{3})$.

Now, considering incident radiation of the same wavelength ( $λ$ ).

Since energy $E=\frac{hc}{λ}$, the incident energy is the same for all three metals.

Substituting this into the energy equation:

$\mathrm{K}_{\max }=\mathrm{E}_{\text{incident}}-\Phi _{0}$

Since $\mathrm{E}_{\text{incident}}$ is constant, the metal with the smallest work function ( $\Phi _{0}$ ) will result in the greatest kinetic energy ( $\mathrm{K}_{\text{\max }}$ ).

As metal $\mathrm{X}_{1}$ has the lowest threshold frequency and thus the lowest work function, it will emit electrons with the greatest kinetic energy. 

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text: A slit of width $a$ is illuminated by light of wavelength $λ$. The linear separation between $1^{\text{st}}$ and $3^{\text{rd}}$ minima in the diffraction pattern produced on a screen placed at a distance $D$ from the slit system is $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a slit of width a , the condition for the $\mathrm{n}^{\text{th}}$ order minimum is that the path difference between the extreme rays is an integral multiple of the wavelength ( $λ$ ) :

$\mathrm{a}\sin θ_{\mathrm{n}}=\mathrm{n}λ$

Where $\mathrm{n}=1,2,3,\ldots$

For small angles of diffraction $(θ_{n})$, we can approximate $\sin θ_{n}\approx θ_{n}$. Thus: $θ_{n}\approx \frac{nλ}{a}$

The linear distance $(y_{n})$ of the $n^{\text{th}}$ minimum from the central maximum on a screen at distance $D$ is given by :


[IMG]


$\mathrm{y}_{\mathrm{n}}=\mathrm{D}\tan θ_{\mathrm{n}}\approx \mathrm{D}θ_{\mathrm{n}}$

Substituting the value of $θ_{\mathrm{n}}$ :

$\mathrm{y}_{\mathrm{n}}=\frac{\mathrm{nD}λ}{\mathrm{a}}$

We need to find the linear separation between the $1^{\text{st}}$ minimum and the $3^{\text{rd}}$ minimum on the same side of the central maximum.

Position of $1^{\text{st}}$ minimum ( $\mathrm{n}=1$ ): $\mathrm{y}_{1}=\frac{1\cdot \mathrm{D}λ}{\mathrm{a}}$

Position of $3^{\mathrm{rd}}$ minimum $(\mathrm{n}=3):\mathrm{y}_{3}=\frac{3\cdot \mathrm{D}λ}{\mathrm{a}}$

The linear separation ( $\Delta y$ ) is :

$\Delta \mathrm{y}=\mathrm{y}_{3}-\mathrm{y}_{1}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta \mathrm{y}=\frac{3\mathrm{D}λ}{\mathrm{a}}-\frac{\mathrm{D}λ}{\mathrm{a}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta \mathrm{y}=\frac{2\mathrm{D}λ}{\mathrm{a}}$

Therefore, the correct option is (C).

text:
A string $A$ of length 0.314 m and Young's modulus $2\times 10^{10}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}^{2}$ is connected to another string $B$ of length and Young's modulus both twice of those of $A$. This series combination of strings is then suspended from a rigid support and its free end is fixed to a load of mass 0.8 kg . The net change in length of the combination is $____$ mm.

(radius of both the strings is 0.2 mm and acceleration due to gravity $=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$ ) (Mass of both strings is to be neglected as compared to the mass of load)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Young's Modulus is defined as the ratio of longitudinal stress $(σ)$ to longitudinal strain $(𝜖)$ :

$\mathrm{Y}=\frac{σ}{𝜖}=\frac{\mathrm{F}/\mathrm{A}}{\Delta \mathrm{L}/\mathrm{L}}$

$\Delta \mathrm{L}=\frac{\mathrm{FL}}{\mathrm{AY}}$

Where :

F is the tension in the string ( $\mathrm{F}=\mathrm{mg}$ for a suspended load).

L is the original length.

A is the cross-sectional area ( $πr^{2}$ ).

Y is the Young's Modulus.


[IMG]


For String A

The length of string is $L_{A}=0.314\mathrm{m}\approx \frac{π}{10}\mathrm{m}$

Young's modulus is $Y_{A}=2\times 10^{10}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}^{2}$

The radius of wire is $\mathrm{r}=0.2\mathrm{mm}=2\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{m}$

So, the area of string A is $\mathrm{A}=π\left (2\times 10^{-4}\right )^{2}=4π\times 10^{-8}\mathrm{m}^{2}$

The tensile force is $\mathrm{F}=\mathrm{mg}=0.8\times 10=8\mathrm{N}$

So, the elongation in string A is,

$\Delta \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{A}}=\frac{8\times 0.314}{\left (4π\times 10^{-8}\right )\times \left (2\times 10^{10}\right )}$

Using $0.314\approx \frac{π}{10}$ :

$\Delta \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{A}}=\frac{8\times \left (\frac{π}{10}\right )}{8π\times 10^{2}}=\frac{π}{10\times π\times 10^{2}}=10^{-3}\mathrm{m}=1\mathrm{mm}$

For string B

It is given that $L_{B}=2L_{A}$ and $Y_{B}=2Y_{A}$, while $F$ and $A$ remain the same:

$\Delta L_{B}=\frac{F(2L_{A})}{A(2Y_{A})}=\frac{FL_{A}}{AY_{A}}=\Delta L_{A}$

So, $\Delta \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{B}}=1\mathrm{mm}$.

Hence, the total elongation of the combination is,

$\Delta \mathrm{L}_{\text{total}}=\Delta \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{A}}+\Delta \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{B}}=1\mathrm{mm}+1\mathrm{mm}=2\mathrm{mm}$

Therefore, the correct option is (B).

text: One gas of $n_{1}$ mole of molecules at temperature $T_{1}$, volume $V_{1}$, and pressure $P_{1}$, and another gas of $n_{2}$ mole of molecules at temperature $T_{2}$, volume $V_{2}$, and pressure $P_{2}$, are mixed resulting in pressure $P$ and volume $V$ of the mixture. The temperature of the mixture is $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The ideal gas law is given by: $\mathrm{PV}=\mathrm{nRT}\Rightarrow \mathrm{n}=\frac{\mathrm{PV}}{\mathrm{RT}}$

Where R is the universal gas constant.

For the first gas : $\mathrm{n}_{1}=\frac{\mathrm{P}_{1}\mathrm{V}_{1}}{\mathrm{R}\mathrm{T}_{1}}$

For the second gas : $\mathrm{n}_{2}=\frac{\mathrm{P}_{2}\mathrm{V}_{2}}{\mathrm{R}\mathrm{T}_{2}}$

When the gases are mixed, the total number of moles $n$ is the sum of the individual moles :

$\mathrm{n}=\mathrm{n}_{1}+\mathrm{n}_{2}$

Using the ideal gas law for the final mixture (pressure P , volume V , and temperature T ) :

$\frac{PV}{RT}=\frac{P_{1}V_{1}}{RT_{1}}+\frac{P_{2}V_{2}}{RT_{2}}$

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{PV}{T}=\dfrac{P_{1}V_{1}}{T_{1}}+\dfrac{P_{2}V_{2}}{T_{2}} \\ \dfrac{PV}{T}=\dfrac{P_{1}V_{1}T_{2}+P_{2}V_{2}T_{1}}{T_{1}T_{2}} \\ \dfrac{T}{PV}=\dfrac{T_{1}T_{2}}{P_{1}V_{1}T_{2}+P_{2}V_{2}T_{1}} \\ T=\dfrac{T_{1}T_{2}PV}{P_{1}V_{1}T_{2}+P_{2}V_{2}T_{1}} \end{array}$

Therefore, the temperature of the mixture of two gases is $\frac{\mathrm{T}_{1}\mathrm{T}_{2}\mathrm{PV}}{\mathrm{P}_{1}\mathrm{V}_{1}\mathrm{T}_{2}+\mathrm{P}_{2}\mathrm{V}_{2}\mathrm{T}_{1}}$. 

Thus, the correct option is (B).

text:
An ideal gas undergoes a process maintaining relation between pressure $(P)$ and $\mathrm{volume}(V)$ as $P=P_{\mathrm{o}}\left (1+\left (\frac{V_{\mathrm{o}}}{V}\right )^{2}\right )^{-1}$, where $P_{\mathrm{o}}$ and $V_{\mathrm{o}}$ are constants. If two samples $A$ and $B$ (two moles each) with initial volumes $V_{\mathrm{o}}$ and $3V_{\mathrm{o}}$ respectively undergo above mentioned process and attain same pressure, then the difference at the temperatures of these samples, $T_{B}-T_{A}$ is $____$ .

( $R=$ gas constant)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From the ideal gas law

$\mathrm{PV}=\mathrm{nRT}\Rightarrow \mathrm{T}=\frac{\mathrm{PV}}{\mathrm{nR}}$

The process for the given gas is $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{o}}\left (1+\left (\frac{\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{o}}}{\mathrm{V}}\right )^{2}\right )^{-1}$

Substituting the given expression for P :

$P=\frac{P_{0}}{1+\frac{V2 0}{V2}}=\frac{P_{0}V^{2}}{V^{2}+V_{0}^{2}}$

Now, substituting this P into the temperature equation :

$T=\frac{1}{nR}\left (\frac{P_{0}V^{2}}{V^{2}+V_{0}^{2}}\right )V=\frac{P_{0}V^{3}}{nR\left (V^{2}+V_{0}^{2}\right )}$

For sample A , the volume is $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{A}}=\mathrm{V}_{0}$ and the number of moles $\mathrm{n}=2$.

$T_{A}=\frac{P_{0}(V_{0})^{3}}{2R\left (V_{0}^{2}+V_{0}^{2}\right )}=\frac{P_{0}V_{0}^{3}}{2R\left (2V_{0}^{2}\right )}=\frac{P_{0}V_{0}}{4R}$

For sample B , the volume is $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{B}}=3\mathrm{V}_{0}$ and $\mathrm{n}=2$.

$T_{B}=\frac{P_{0}(3V_{0})^{3}}{2R\left ((3V_{0})^{2}+V_{0}^{2}\right )}=\frac{P_{0}\left (27V_{0}^{3}\right )}{2R\left (9V_{0}^{2}+V_{0}^{2}\right )}=\frac{27P_{0}V_{0}^{3}}{2R\left (10V_{0}^{2}\right )}=\frac{27P_{0}V_{0}}{20R}$

So, the temperature difference is,

$T_{B}-T_{A}=\frac{27P_{0}V_{0}}{20R}-\frac{P_{0}V_{0}}{4R}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{B}}-\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{A}}=\frac{27\mathrm{P}_{0}\mathrm{V}_{0}-5\mathrm{P}_{0}\mathrm{V}_{0}}{20\mathrm{R}}=\frac{22\mathrm{P}_{0}\mathrm{V}_{0}}{20\mathrm{R}}=\frac{11\mathrm{P}_{0}\mathrm{V}_{0}}{10\mathrm{R}}$

Therefore, the correct option is (B).

text: A voltmeter with internal resistance of $x\Omega$ can be used to measure upto 20 V . In order to increase its measuring range to 30 V , the required modification is to $____$ .
options: connect resistor of $\frac{x}{2}\Omega$, in series with voltmeter.
connect resistor of $\frac{x}{2}\Omega$, in parallel to voltmeter.
connect a resistor of $x\Omega$ in series with voltmeter.
connect resistor of $2x\Omega$ in parallel to voltmeter.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A voltmeter is a galvanometer with a high resistance connected in series. To increase the range of an existing voltmeter, we must add more resistance in series.

Let the full-scale deflection current of the voltmeter be $\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{g}}$.


[IMG]


Initially, the voltmeter has a resistance x and measures up to $\mathrm{V}_{1}=20\mathrm{V}$.

According to Ohm's Law ( $\mathrm{V}=\mathrm{IR}$ ):

$20=I_{g}\cdot x\Rightarrow I_{g}=\frac{20}{x}$

To measure a new maximum voltage $\mathrm{V}_{2}=30\mathrm{V}$, we connect an additional resistance R in series with the voltmeter.


[IMG]


The total resistance becomes $(x+R)$. The current required for full-scale deflection remains $I_{g}$ :

$V_{2}=I_{g}(x+R)$

Substituting $\mathrm{V}_{2}=30$ and $\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{g}}=\frac{20}{\mathrm{x}}$ into the equation :

$30=\left (\frac{20}{x}\right )(x+R)$

$\Rightarrow$ $3=\frac{2}{x}(x+R)$

$\Rightarrow$ $3x=2(x+R)$

$\Rightarrow$ $3x=2x+2R$

$\Rightarrow$ $x=2R\Rightarrow R=\frac{x}{2}\Omega$

Thus, to increase the range to 30 V , a resistor of value $\frac{x}{2}\Omega$ must be connected in series with the voltmeter. 

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
A rod of length 10 cm lies along the principle axis of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm as shown in figure. The length of the image is $____$ cm.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Using mirror formula,

$\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{v}+\frac{1}{u}$

Where, the focal length is f , object distance is u , and image distance is v .

According to the sign convention for a concave mirror:

Focal length $\mathrm{f}=-10\mathrm{cm}$

Distances measured in the direction of incident light are positive; opposite is negative.

The end of the rod closer to the mirror is at a distance of 20 cm from the pole.


[IMG]


$\mathrm{u}_{1}=-20\mathrm{cm}$

Using mirror formula for point A,

$\frac{1}{-10}=\frac{1}{v_{1}}+\frac{1}{-20}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{v_{1}}=\frac{1}{20}-\frac{1}{10}=\frac{1-2}{20}=-\frac{1}{20}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{v}_{1}=-20\mathrm{cm}$

Since $\mathrm{u}=2\mathrm{f}=\mathrm{R}$ (the center of curvature), the image is formed at the same location ( $\mathrm{v}=-20\mathrm{cm}$ ).

The rod has a length of 10 cm and extends away from the mirror. Therefore, the far end $(\mathrm{B})$ is at :

$\mathrm{u}_{2}=-(20+10)=-30\mathrm{cm}$

Using mirror formula for point B ,

$\frac{1}{-10}=\frac{1}{v_{2}}+\frac{1}{-30}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{v_{2}}=\frac{1}{30}-\frac{1}{10}=\frac{1-3}{30}=-\frac{2}{30}=-\frac{1}{15}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{v}_{2}=-15\mathrm{cm}$

The length of the image is the magnitude of the difference between the two image positions:

Length $=|\mathrm{v}_{1}-\mathrm{v}_{2}|$

Length $=|-20-(-15)|=|-5|=5\mathrm{cm}$

Therefore, the length of image of the rod is 5 cm . 

Thus, the correct option is (B).

text: A parallel plate air capacitor is connected to a battery. The plates are pulled apart at uniform speed $v$. If $x$ is the separation between the plates at any instant, then the time rate of change of electrostatic energy of the capacitor is proportional to $x^{α}$, where $α$ is $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The electrostatic energy $(U)$ stored in a capacitor connected to a battery of constant voltage $V$ is given by :

$\mathrm{U}=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{CV}^{2}$

The capacitance $(\mathrm{C})$ of a parallel plate capacitor with plate area A and separation x is :

$\mathrm{C}=\frac{𝜖_{0}\mathrm{A}}{\mathrm{x}}$

Substituting into the energy formula :

$U=\frac{1}{2}\left (\frac{𝜖_{0}A}{x}\right )V^{2}=\frac{𝜖_{0}AV^{2}}{2x}$

We need to find the time rate of change of energy, which is the derivative of $U$ with respect to time ( $t$ ) :

$\frac{\mathrm{dU}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{dt}}\left (\frac{𝜖_{0}\mathrm{AV}^{2}}{2\mathrm{x}}\right )$

Since $𝜖_{0},\mathrm{A}$, and $V$ are constants :

$\frac{dU}{dt}=\frac{𝜖_{0}AV^{2}}{2}\frac{d}{dt}\left (\frac{1}{x}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{dU}{dt}=\frac{𝜖_{0}AV^{2}}{2}\left (-\frac{1}{x^{2}}\right )\frac{dx}{dt}$

The plates are pulled apart at a uniform speed v , which means $\frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\mathrm{v}$ (a constant).

$\frac{dU}{dt}=-\left (\frac{𝜖_{0}AV^{2}v}{2}\right )\frac{1}{x^{2}}$

So, the rate of change of energy is proportional to $\frac{1}{x^{2}}$ :

$\frac{dU}{dt}\propto x^{-2}\Rightarrow x^{-2}=x^{a}\Rightarrow a=-2$

Therefore, the value of a is -2 . 

Thus, the correct option is (A).

text: An insulated wire is wound so that it forms a flat coil with $N=200$ turns. The radius of the innermost turn is $r_{1}=3\mathrm{cm}$, and of the outermost turn $r_{2}=6\mathrm{cm}$. If 20 mA current flows in it then the magnetic moment will be $α\times 10^{-2}\mathrm{A}.\mathrm{m}^{2}$. The value of $α$ is $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a single circular turn of radius $r$ carrying current $I$, the magnetic moment is :

$\mathrm{m}=\mathrm{I}\cdot \mathrm{A}=\mathrm{I}\left (π\mathrm{r}^{2}\right )$

In a flat coil where the turns are wound from $\mathrm{r}_{1}$ to $\mathrm{r}_{2}$, the number of turns per unit radial length is $\mathrm{n}=\frac{\mathrm{N}}{\mathrm{r}_{2}-\mathrm{r}_{1}}$. The total magnetic moment ( M ) is the integral of the moments of all infinitesimal turns of thickness dr :

$M=\int\limits _{r_{1}}^{r_{2}}\left (Iπr^{2}\right )\cdot ndr$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{M}=\mathrm{I}π\mathrm{n}\int\limits _{\mathrm{r}_{1}}^{\mathrm{r}_{2}}\mathrm{r}^{2}\mathrm{dr}=\mathrm{I}π\left (\frac{\mathrm{N}}{\mathrm{r}_{2}-\mathrm{r}_{1}}\right )\left [\frac{\mathrm{r}^{3}}{3}\right ]_{\mathrm{r}_{1}}^{\mathrm{r}_{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{M}=\frac{\mathrm{NI}π}{3(\mathrm{r}_{2}-\mathrm{r}_{1})}\left (\mathrm{r}_{2}^{3}-\mathrm{r}_{1}^{3}\right )$

Using the algebraic identity $r_{2}^{3}-r_{1}^{3}=(r_{2}-r_{1})\left (r_{2}^{2}+r_{1}^{2}+r_{1}r_{2}\right )$ :

$\mathrm{M}=\frac{\mathrm{NI}π}{3}\left (\mathrm{r}_{1}^{2}+\mathrm{r}_{2}^{2}+\mathrm{r}_{1}\mathrm{r}_{2}\right )$

Substituting the values, where number of turns is $\mathrm{N}=200$, the current is $\mathrm{I}=20\mathrm{mA}=20\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{A}$, the inner radius of coil is $\mathrm{r}_{1}=3\mathrm{cm}=0.03\mathrm{m}$ and the outer radius is $\mathrm{r}_{2}=6\mathrm{cm}=0.06\mathrm{m}$

$\mathrm{M}=\frac{200\times 20\times 10^{-3}\times 3.14}{3}\left (0.03^{2}+0.06^{2}+0.03\times 0.06\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $M=\frac{4\times 3.14}{3}(0.0009+0.0036+0.0018)$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{M}=\frac{12.56}{3}(0.0063)=12.56\times 0.0021$

$\Rightarrow$ $M=0.026376\approx 2.64\times 10^{-2}A.m^{2}=α\times 10^{-2}A.m^{2}\Rightarrow α=2.64$

Therefore, the value of $α$ is 2.64 . 

Thus, the correct option is (B).

Consider a circuit consisting of a capacitor $(20μ\mathrm{F})$, resistor $(100\Omega )$ and two identical diodes as shown in figure. The resistance of diode under forward biasing condition is $10\Omega$. The time constant of the circuit is $α\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{s}$. The value of $α$ is $____$

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the given circuit, the two diodes are connected in parallel but with opposite polarities. When a DC voltage V is applied,


[IMG]


Diode $\mathrm{D}_{1}$ will be forward biased, acting as a closed switch with resistance $10\Omega$.

The other diode $\mathrm{D}_{2}$ will be reverse biased, acting as an open switch with infinite resistance.

Therefore, only one diode branch conducts current at any given time.

The resultant circuit is,


[IMG]


The circuit is a series combination of the capacitor ( C ), the main resistor ( R ), and the forward-biased diode resistance ( $R_{d}$ ).

$\mathrm{R}_{\text{total}}=\mathrm{R}+\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{d}}$

Given $\mathrm{R}=100\Omega$ and $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{d}}=10\Omega$ :

$\mathrm{R}_{\text{total}}=100+10=110\Omega$

The time constant of an RC circuit is defined as the product of the total resistance and the capacitance:

$τ=\mathrm{R}_{\text{total}}\times \mathrm{C}$

The capacitance is given as $\mathrm{C}=20μ\mathrm{F}=20\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{F}$ :

$τ=110\times \left (20\times 10^{-6}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $τ=2200\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{s}$

$\Rightarrow$ $τ=2.2\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{s}=α\times 10^{-3}$

$\Rightarrow α=2.2.$

Therefore, the correct option is (A).

The voltage and the current between $A$ and $B$ points shown in the circuit are $____$ .


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The circuit consists of four parallel branches between points A and B :

Branch 1: $\mathrm{E}_{1}=27\mathrm{V},\mathrm{r}_{1}=3\Omega$

Branch 2: $\mathrm{E}_{2}=27\mathrm{V},\mathrm{r}_{2}=3\Omega$

Branch 3: Two cells in series ( 14 V and 13 V ) and a resistor. The total EMF is $\mathrm{E}_{3}=14+13=27\mathrm{V},\mathrm{r}_{3}=3\Omega$

Branch 4: $\mathrm{E}_{4}=27\mathrm{V},\mathrm{r}_{4}=3\Omega$


[IMG]


Since all branches have the same EMF ( 27 V ) and are connected in parallel with the same polarity, the equivalent EMF of the combination is

$\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{eq}}=\frac{\frac{\mathrm{E}1}{\mathrm{r}1}+\frac{\mathrm{E}2}{\mathrm{r}2}+\frac{\mathrm{E}3}{\mathrm{r}3}+\frac{\mathrm{E}4}{\mathrm{r}4}}{\frac{1}{\mathrm{r}1}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{r}2}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{r}3}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{r}4}}=\frac{\frac{27}{3}+\frac{27}{3}+\frac{27}{3}+\frac{27}{3}}{\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3}}=27\mathrm{V}$

The four $3\Omega$ resistors are in parallel. The equivalent internal resistance is :

$\frac{1}{\mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{eq}}}=\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3}=\frac{4}{3}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{eq}}=\frac{3}{4}\Omega =0.75\Omega$

So, the equivalent circuit is,


[IMG]


Between points A and B , the load consisting of two $3\Omega$ resistors in series.

So, total external resistance $\mathrm{R}=3+3=6\Omega$.

The total current (i) in the circuit is :

$i=\frac{E_{eq}}{R+r_{eq}}=\frac{27}{6+0.75}=\frac{27}{6.75}=4\mathrm{A}$

The terminal voltage ( $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{AB}}$ ) across points A and B is :

$V_{AB}=E_{eq}-\mathrm{ir}_{\mathrm{eq}}\text{or}V_{AB}=\mathrm{I}\times \mathrm{R}$

$\Rightarrow$ $V_{AB}=4\times 6=24\mathrm{V}$

Therefore, the voltage is 24 V and the current is 4 A . 

Thus, the correct option is (B).

text:
An unpolarized light is incident on the plane interface of air-dielectric medium shown in figure. If the incident angle is equal to Brewster angle, identify the expression representing reflected wave.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Brewster's Law states that when unpolarized light strikes a transparent medium at a specific angle called the Brewster angle $(θ_{\mathrm{p}})$, the reflected light becomes completely plane-polarized. At this angle, the reflected ray and the refracted ray are perpendicular to each other.

For light incident at the Brewster angle, the reflected wave is polarized with its electric field vector (E) oscillating perpendicular to the plane of incidence. The plane of incidence is defined by the incident ray and the normal to the surface.

From the diagram, the interface lies in the $\mathrm{xy}-$ plane $(\mathrm{z}=0)$. The incident light is traveling in the xz -plane

The normal to the surface is the z-axis.

Since the plane of incidence is the xz-plane, the electric field of the reflected light must be perpendicular to this plane, which means it must oscillate along the y -axis (direction $\hat{\mathrm{j}}$ ).

A wave equation for an electromagnetic wave is generally represented as

$\vec{\mathrm{E}}=\vec{\mathrm{E}}_{0}\sin (\vec{\mathrm{k}}\cdot \vec{\mathrm{r}}-ω\mathrm{t})$

The reflected wave will be traveling back into the air (positive x and negative z direction relative to the interface).


[IMG]


So, in reflected rays the electric field should only have components perpendicular to the plane of incidence.

So, from the options, we need an expression where the electric field components perpendicular to the plane of incident rays.

Option (A) describes a wave with components $\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{x}}$ and $\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{y}}$. 

Therefore, the correct option is (A).

text: A 1 kg block subjected to two simultaneous forces $(2\hat{\mathrm{i}}+3\hat{\mathrm{j}}+4\hat{\mathrm{k}})\mathrm{N}$ and $(3\hat{\mathrm{i}}-\hat{\mathrm{j}}-2\hat{\mathrm{k}})\mathrm{N}$ is moved a distance of 25 m along $(3\hat{\mathrm{i}}-4\hat{\mathrm{j}})$ direction. The work done in this process is $____$ J.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When multiple forces act on a body simultaneously, the net force is the vector sum of all individual forces :

$\vec{\mathrm{F}}_{\mathrm{net}}=\vec{\mathrm{F}}_{1}+\vec{\mathrm{F}}_{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\vec{\mathrm{F}}_{\mathrm{net}}=(2\hat{ı}+3\hat{ȷ}+4\hat{\mathrm{k}})+(3\hat{ı}-\hat{ȷ}-2\hat{\mathrm{k}})$

$\Rightarrow$ $\vec{\mathrm{F}}_{\mathrm{net}}=(2+3)\hat{ı}+(3-1)\hat{ȷ}+(4-2)\hat{\mathrm{k}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\vec{\mathrm{F}}_{net}=(5\hat{ı}+2\hat{ȷ}+2\hat{\mathrm{k}})\mathrm{N}$

The block moves a distance of 25 m along the direction of the vector $\vec{\mathrm{A}}=3\hat{ı}-4\hat{ȷ}$. The unit vector in this direction is :

$\hat{u}=\frac{⃗{A}}{|⃗{A}|}=\frac{3\hat{ı}-4\hat{ȷ}}{\sqrt{3^{2}+(-4)^{2}}}=\frac{3\hat{ı}-4\hat{ȷ}}{\sqrt{9+16}}=\frac{3\hat{ı}-4\hat{ȷ}}{5}$

The displacement vector $\vec{\mathrm{d}}$ is

$\vec{\mathrm{d}}=25\times \left (\frac{3\hat{ı}-4\hat{ȷ}}{5}\right )=5(3\hat{ı}-4\hat{ȷ})=(15\hat{ı}-20\hat{ȷ})\mathrm{m}$

Work done is defined as the dot product of the force vector and the displacement vector :

$\mathrm{W}=\vec{\mathrm{F}}_{\mathrm{net}}\cdot \mathrm{d}\leftarrow$

$\Rightarrow$ $W=(5\hat{ı}+2\hat{ȷ}+2\hat{k})\cdot (15\hat{ı}-20\hat{ȷ}+0\hat{k})$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{W}=(5\times 15)+(2\times (-20))+(2\times 0)$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{W}=75-40+0=35\mathrm{J}$

Therefore, the correct answer is 35 .
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text:
The surface tension of a soap solution is $3.5\times 10^{-2}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}$. The work required to increase the radius of a soap bubble from 1 cm to 2 cm is $α\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{J}$. The value of $α$ is $____$ .

$(π=22/7)$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A soap bubble has two free surfaces (an inner surface and an outer surface). The surface energy (U) of a bubble with radius r and surface tension T is:

$\mathrm{U}=\mathrm{T}\times \text{(Total Surface Area)}$

$\Rightarrow$ $U=T\times \left (2\times 4πr^{2}\right )=8πr^{2}T$

The work done $(W)$ in increasing the radius from $r_{1}$ to $r_{2}$ is equal to the increase in surface energy:

$\mathrm{W}=\Delta \mathrm{U}=8π\mathrm{T}\left (\mathrm{r}_{2}^{2}-\mathrm{r}_{1}^{2}\right )$

The surface tension of soap solution is given as $\mathrm{T}=3.5\times 10^{-2}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}$

The initial radius of soap bubble is $\mathrm{r}_{1}=1\mathrm{cm}=10^{-2}\mathrm{m}$

The final radius of soap bubble is $\mathrm{r}_{2}=2\mathrm{cm}=2\times 10^{-2}\mathrm{m}$

And the value of $π=22/7$

Putting the values,

$\mathrm{W}=8\times \frac{22}{7}\times \left (3.5\times 10^{-2}\right )\times \left [\left (2\times 10^{-2}\right )^{2}-\left (10^{-2}\right )^{2}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow$ $W=8\times 22\times \left (0.5\times 10^{-2}\right )\times \left [4\times 10^{-4}-1\times 10^{-4}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow$ $W=176\times 0.005\times \left (3\times 10^{-4}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $W=0.88\times 3\times 10^{-4}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{W}=2.64\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{J}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{W}=264\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{J}=α\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{J}$

$\Rightarrow α=264$

Therefore, the value of $α$ is 264 . 

Thus, the correct answer is 264 .
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text: The velocity of a particle executing simple harmonic motion along $x$-axis is described as $v^{2}=50-x^{2}$, where $x$ represents displacement. If the time period of motion is $\frac{x}{7}\mathrm{s}$, the value of $x$ is $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a particle executing SHM with amplitude A and angular frequency $ω$, the velocity v at a displacement x from the mean position is given by relation,

$v^{2}=ω^{2}\left (A^{2}-x^{2}\right )$

The given equation is $\mathrm{v}^{2}=50-\mathrm{x}^{2}$

$v^{2}=1\left (50-x^{2}\right )$

By comparing the two equations,

$ω^{2}=1\Rightarrow ω=1\mathrm{rad}/\mathrm{s}$

$\Rightarrow$ $A^{2}=50\Rightarrow A=\sqrt{50}\text{units}$

The time period T is related to the angular frequency $ω$ by the formula:

$\mathrm{T}=\frac{2π}{ω}$

Substituting $ω=1$ :

$\mathrm{T}=2π\text{seconds}$

$\Rightarrow$ $T=2\times \left (\frac{22}{7}\right )=\frac{44}{7}\text{seconds}=\frac{x}{7}\text{seconds}$

$\Rightarrow x=44$

Therefore, the correct answer is 44 .
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text: A body of mass 2 kg begins to move under the influence of time dependent force $\vec{\mathrm{F}}=\left (2\mathrm{t}\hat{\mathrm{i}}+6\mathrm{t}^{2}\hat{\mathrm{j}}\right )\mathrm{N}$, where $\hat{\mathrm{i}}$ and $\hat{\mathrm{j}}$ are unit vectors along $x$ and y -axis respectively. The power produced by the force at $t=2\mathrm{s}$ is $____$ W.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Power (P) is defined as the rate at which work is done. It can be calculated as the dot product of the force vector $(\vec{\mathrm{F}})$ and the velocity vector $(\vec{\mathrm{V}})$.

According to Newton's Second Law $(⃗{F}=m⃗{a})$, the acceleration is :

$\vec{\mathrm{a}}=\frac{\vec{\mathrm{F}}}{\mathrm{m}}=\frac{2\mathrm{t}\hat{ı}+6\mathrm{t}^{2}\hat{ȷ}}{2}$

$\vec{\mathrm{a}}=\left (\mathrm{t}\hat{ı}+3\mathrm{t}^{2}\hat{ȷ}\right )\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$

Velocity is the integral of acceleration with respect to time. Since the body begins to move, we assume the initial velocity is zero at $\mathrm{t}=0$ :

$⃗{v}=\int ⃗{a}dt=\int\limits _{0}^{t}\left (t\hat{ı}+3t^{2}\hat{ȷ}\right )dt$

$⃗{v}=\left (\frac{t^{2}}{2}\right )\hat{ı}+\left (\frac{3t^{3}}{3}\right )\hat{ȷ}=\left (\frac{t^{2}}{2}\right )\hat{ı}+t^{3}\hat{ȷ}$

Force at $\mathrm{t}=2$ :

$\vec{\mathrm{F}}(2)=[2(2)]\hat{i}+\left [6(2)^{2}\right ]\hat{ȷ}=(4\hat{i}+24\hat{ȷ})\mathrm{N}$

Velocity at $\mathrm{t}=2$ :

$⃗{v}(2)=\left [\frac{(2)^{2}}{2}\right ]\hat{ı}+(2)^{3}\hat{ȷ}=(2\hat{ı}+8\hat{ȷ})\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$

So, the power at $\mathrm{t}=2\mathrm{s}$ is,

$\mathrm{P}=\vec{\mathrm{F}}\cdot \vec{\mathrm{v}}$

$\begin{array}{l} P=(4\hat{ı}+24\hat{ȷ})\cdot (2\hat{ı}+8\hat{ȷ}) \\ P=(4\times 2)+(24\times 8) \\ P=8+192=200\mathrm{W} \end{array}$

Therefore, the correct answer is 200 .

text: An inductor of 10 mH , capacitor of $0.1μ\mathrm{F}$ and a resistor of $100\Omega$ are connected in series across an $a.c$ power supply $220\mathrm{V},70\mathrm{Hz}$. The power factor of the given circuit is 0.5 . The difference in the inductive reactance and capacitance reactance is $\sqrt{3}α\Omega$. The value of $α$ is $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In a series LCR circuit, the impedance ( $Z$ ) is the vector sum of the resistance ( $R$ ), inductive reactance ( $X_{L}$ ), and capacitive reactance $(\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}})$.
